steps.decide: Which questions the dashboard answers in its first viewport, and which widgets merely display data
How each widget reports its own loading, empty and failure without taking the page down
How reserved space prevents the layout from jumping while numbers arrive
How a widget is opened, filtered and reordered by keyboard alone
How zero differs from no data, and what each says

rules.statement: A widget earns its space by answering a question the operator acts on; a metric nobody has ever clicked through to is removed from the first viewport rather than shrunk.
Each widget loads, fails and retries on its own; one failing query never blanks the dashboard or blocks the others.
Every widget reserves its final height before data arrives, so numbers replacing skeletons do not move anything the operator is about to click.
Reordering is available from the keyboard with explicit move actions and announced positions, never drag-only.
Zero and no-data are different: zero is measured and reads as 0 with its period, no data says that nothing was collected and why.
A refresh announces which widget updated and when, without moving focus or re-reading the whole grid.

stateMachine.staleResponseRule: a widget keeps the newest response per filter; responses for an abandoned filter are dropped by sequence number and never repaint the widget

transitions.trigger: the widget's range or filter changes

motion.motion: skeleton shimmers in place over 200ms, never changing size
motion.reducedMotion: a static placeholder with the same dimensions replaces shimmer
values swap instantly; the live region announces the new value

motion.motion: the widget's own error appears over 120ms inside its frame
motion.reducedMotion: the error appears instantly inside the same frame

transitions.trigger: the operator drills into a segment

motion.motion: the selected segment brightens over 100ms and the rest dim
motion.reducedMotion: the selection changes instantly with no dimming

motion.motion: the widget returns to its full range over 120ms

transitions.trigger: Retry is pressed inside the widget

motion.motion: the error hands back to the skeleton over 120ms

transitions.trigger: the widget's data source is not entitled for this workspace

motion.noneReason: an entitlement boundary is a fact, not a transition; the frame stays and states what is missing

motion.motion: the focus ring disappears with no delay
motion.reducedMotion: identical — the ring is immediate in both cases

motion.noneReason: returning permission restores operability; a control does not animate its own permissions

refused.reason: a single figure has nothing to select; drill-down is the chart's job
a chart with no entitlement is not rendered at all rather than shown inert
a list has no success state; the rows themselves are the result

sections.intent: Answer the three or four questions an operator opens the product with, and keep answering them honestly when one source is slow, empty or broken.
useCases: drill into one segment to see what changed
reorder the grid so the morning check is first
nicheDifferences: A dashboard is opened many times a day by the same person; novelty is worthless and stability is everything. Widgets therefore behave like instruments, not cards.
inputs: the questions the operator actually acts on
the freshness and latency of each source
the entitlements that gate each widget
the widest realistic label and value per widget
anatomy: a grid with reserved height per widget
a per-widget frame carrying title, period and refresh time
a reorder affordance usable by keyboard
styling: figures use tabular numerals so digits do not jitter between refreshes
the grid keeps one accent for the current period and neutral tone for comparisons
borders define frames; shadows are not used to imply elevation the grid does not have
a11y: each widget is a labelled region with its title as the accessible name
values and periods are exposed as text, not only inside a canvas or SVG
refreshes announce through a polite live region naming the widget and the time
reordering uses explicit move buttons with announced positions
responsive: below 768 px the grid becomes one column in priority order, never a horizontal scroller
charts keep a minimum height of 160 px and re-render to the narrower width instead of being cropped
the period selector becomes a single control that states the active range
copy: each widget states its period and last update time
empty data says what was not collected and why, and offers the action that would start collecting
errors name the source and the retry, never 'Unable to load'
alternatives: a single question-first page when the operator needs one answer, not a grid
an exported report for weekly review instead of a live dashboard
alerting when the number matters more than watching it

acceptance: each widget loads, fails and retries independently while the rest stays usable
no widget changes height when data replaces its skeleton
zero renders as 0 with its period and no-data explains the absence
the grid can be reordered with the keyboard and the new position is announced
a refresh announces the widget and time without moving focus
failureCases: one failing query blanks the entire dashboard
skeletons collapse and the operator clicks the wrong widget when numbers arrive
zero is rendered as no-data and the operator believes collection stopped
reordering is drag-only and impossible from the keyboard
